title: Unified admission spec: soft-pin behavior and runtime fallbacks
creator: Maya Chen
description: This PRD clarifies requirements for onboarding new open models into the catalog with a focus on 'soft-pin' semantics, automatic runtime compatibility assertions, and deterministic fallback behavior. Goal: reduce operational surprises when community/open weights are ingested while allowing experiments and rapid exposure for PM/Dev users. This spec sets the acceptance criteria, API contract for catalog metadata, UX cues in the Console, rollout constraints, and runtime guardrails for Dedicated/Hosted/Private deployments.
scope_inclusions: Definition of soft-pin metadata fields and priority semantics (major/minor/variant-level)
Runtime compatibility assertions surfaced from model ingest probes (kernel support, quantization friendliness, KV cache shape)
Fallback routing rules for unpinned or incompatible variants (model alias mapping and explicit fallback chain)
Console UX: ingestion status page, compatibility score, and recommended pinning actions
API additions: intake endpoint fields, ingest validation errors, and compatibility warnings
scope_exclusions: Automated model retraining or fine-tuning during ingest
Changes to billing or quota models for hosted inference
Deep integration with third-party model registries beyond metadata import
acceptance_criteria: Catalog ingest accepts new open-model submissions with a soft_pin boolean and optional pin_scope string; missing soft_pin defaults to true
Ingest pipeline runs runtime probes (binary kernel compatibility, FP/quant support, KV cache estimate) and returns a compatibility_score between 0-100
Models with compatibility_score < 40 are flagged as 'incompatible' and blocked from auto-serving in hosted tier until a soft-approval is recorded
Soft-pinned variants can be rolled out to Dedicated and Private customers but must include an explicit fallback chain to a verified pinned variant for automated routing failure modes
Console surfaces a clear action card with recommended pin level (unpin/pin-major/pin-variant), compatibility reasons, and one-click pin workflow
API returns machine-readable warnings that client SDKs consume to enable on-client fallback policies (headers: X-Model-Compat, X-Model-Fallback-Chain)
Runtime respects pin semantics: major pin prevents automatic variant substitution across major-version changes; variant pin prevents substitution entirely
If runtime detects a kernel-incompatibility at serve-time, it must invoke fallback chain within 200ms and increment a catalog-level incident counter
Security review completed and recorded (security_review_required = true) for any model that requests access to private deployments or has native bindings (C++/CUDA) in its artifacts
api_contract: Intake POST /catalog/models accepts: name, upstream_uri, soft_pin (true|false), pin_scope (none|major|variant), suggested_fallbacks (list of model IDs or aliases), provenance (string), license (string), expected_fp (fp32|fp16|int8), kv_cache_estimate (tokens), and submitter_email. Response includes model_id, ingest_status, compatibility_score, compatibility_reasons (list), suggested_pin_level, and warnings (list). Warnings use stable codes. Client-facing GET /catalog/models/:id returns compatibility metadata and current pin state.
ux_requirements: Ingest modal shows compatibility_score with color-coded banding and top-3 reasons
Pin action workflow requires a short justification (<= 250 chars) and records actor + timestamp
A 'safety playground' flag visible to internal users to route experimental unpinned variants to internal-only traffic for 72 hours
Console must show fallback chain visualization and a one-click 'promote fallback to primary' action for admins
Telemetry link from the model page to per-model latency/cost dashboards and recent fallback incidents
evaluation_gates: Sanity tests: generation correctness on baseline prompt set must not regress beyond 5% BLEU/ROUGE delta compared to pinned baseline
Performance tests: median token latency within 1.5x of pinned baseline for same hardware/profile
Resource tests: memory/KV cache estimate must fit the smallest target dedicated shape if target tier is Dedicated-small
Security/License check: license must be compatible with commercial-serving; incompatible license blocks ingest
Unit tests: ingest validation must reject malformed manifests and return clear error codes
runtime_guardrails: On-serve kernel mismatch detection: runtime will compare model runtime signature (ops used, fused-kernel hints) against node kernel capabilities and mark runtime_incompatibility when mismatch occurs
Automated fallback: if runtime_incompatibility or OOM occurs, route request to first available fallback; if no fallback, return structured error with guidance
Telemetry: every fallback increments model.fallback_count and emits a trace with original model_id and fallback_target
KV cache semantics: models that request persistent KV cache larger than node limit must be flagged as incompatible for that node class
Gradual rollout: allow canary percentage + success metric threshold before widening traffic to soft-pinned variant
rollout_steps: Stage 1: Implement API contract and ingest validation (ENG) in a feature branch
Stage 2: Add runtime probes and compatibility scoring backend; expose to internal console (internal-only)
Stage 3: Enable soft-pin ingest for internal teams and QA with safety playground routing
Stage 4: Public beta: allow external users to submit soft-pinned models behind rate limit and require a documented fallback chain
Stage 5: GA: enable default soft-pin behavior for all ingest, add migration tooling for previously unpinned models
notes_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: conservative compatibility threshold reduces incidents but increases manual pinning work for models that are actually usable on some nodes
Tradeoff: exposing compatibility_score may discourage community submissions; mitigate by showing actionable remediation steps
Decision: default soft_pin=true to protect customers who depend on pin semantics; allow opt-out by trusted submitters
Open question: how to canonicalize suggested_fallbacks across tenant boundaries—decision deferred to ENG-4217
